title: Knight Probability in Chessboard
description: Calculate the probability that a knight remains on the board after K moves.
pseudocode:
1: dp = new matrix(n, n, 1)
2: for step = 1 to k:
3:   newDp = new matrix(n, n, 0)
4:   for r, c in cells:
5:     for dr, dc in knightMoves:
6:       if (r+dr, c+dc) is on board:
7:         newDp[r+dr][c+dc] += dp[r][c] / 8
8:   dp = newDp
9: return sum(dp)

steps.note: Initialize 3x3 DP table with probability 1.0 (starting position [1,1])
Initialize next state matrix with zeros
Knight at [1,1] has valid moves to [0,3] (invalid), [3,0] (invalid), etc. Valid: [0,3] no, [2,3] no. For 3x3, most moves go off-board.
Distribute probability 1/8 to each of the 8 possible moves if within bounds
Sum of probabilities is 0 as all moves from [1,1] in 3x3 lead off-board
